html:
Gooty is a town in Andhra Pradesh below one of south India's great hill forts. On the 1783 and 1800 maps it names a small territory around the fort.

The fort was strengthened under Vijayanagara. In the 1700s it was the seat of Murari Rao Ghorpade, a Maratha chief who sold his sword to many sides in the Carnatic wars. Hyder Ali of Mysore took Gooty from him in 1775. After Tipu's defeats it passed to the Nizam, who handed it to the British in 1800 among the Ceded Districts. Their administrator, Thomas Munro, died nearby in 1827 and was first buried at Gooty.
